educationalGoal: ・Familiarize students with the structure and scoring system of the TOEFL exam. ・Provide extensive practice in each of the four sections of the TOEFL: Reading, Listening, Speaking, and Writing. ・Help students build confidence and learn strategies for approaching TOEFL tasks effectively. ・Measure progress through pre/post mock TOEFL tests.
advice: This course is designed for students preparing for the TOEFL exam with minimal experience. Students will engage in interactive activities, practice all four sections of the TOEFL, and learn effective test-taking strategies. The course will include two Integrated Learning (IL) days to encourage collaborative practice and mock tests on Day 1 and Day 14 to measure progress. Attendance, participation, and active engagement in exercises are crucial for success.

activityGoals.body: Ability to understand and apply TOEFL test-taking strategies.
Learn how to manage time effectively during the exam.
Practice writing strategies that are helpful for answer TOEFL writing questions.
Become familiar with the vocabulary and writing styles used on the TOEFL.
Improve listening skills based on typical TOEFL listening questions.
Improve ability to answer speaking questions that frequently appear on TOEFL.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1. Students understand TOEFL structure and scoring. 2. Achieve high scores in all mock tests. 3. Answer all section questions accurately. 4. Use strategies for time management and analysis. 5. Speak fluently with minimal hesitation. 6. Write logically, with well-supported arguments. 7. Actively participate and show progress. 8. Display critical thinking in IL activities.
achievementLevels.standard: 1. Students understand TOEFL structure and scoring. 2. Show moderate improvement in mock test scores. 3. Answer most questions correctly, minor errors. 4. Use basic strategies for time management. 5. Speak clearly with occasional pauses and errors. 6. Write with clear structure, minor grammar issues. 7. Participate in class and complete assignments. 8. Demonstrate basic integration in IL tasks.
